title: Adjuvant trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)

agents.name: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
agents.type: HER2-directed antibody with a chemotherapy payload
agents.mechanism: HER2 targeting carries DM1 into cancer cells.
agents.explanation: The antibody attaches to HER2. After the complex enters a cell, its DM1 payload disrupts structures needed for cell division. This is a single linked medicine, with its own dosing and safety rules.
agents.watch: Report bleeding, numbness, jaundice, new cough or breathlessness. Keep blood and heart checks.

context_label: Adjuvant · residual invasive HER2-positive early breast cancer
purpose: After preoperative treatment and surgery, residual invasive HER2-positive cancer can lead to a change to T-DM1 to reduce recurrence risk.
schedule_summary: T-DM1 by IV infusion every 21 days for 14 postoperative cycles, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.

phases_title: Each phase in your treatment plan
phases_note: The order depends on the indication and your recovery. The whole-treatment map shows how local treatment and ongoing medicines relate to each other.
medicines_title: Your medicines and their different roles
timeline_note: Planned treatment days are distinct from broad possible symptom patterns. Symptoms can occur outside these bands.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Fever, shivers, sudden illness, new breathing problems or severe symptoms need prompt advice on any day, including a treatment break.
teachback: Which medicines are you taking now? What changes in the next phase? Which checks are due and who reviews them before treatment?
consent_support: Discuss the active phase, supportive medicines, fertility / menopause, treatment alternatives, monitoring, urgent contacts and when the plan will be reviewed.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, jaundice, marked bleeding, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, chest symptoms or a severe rash promptly.

support.title: Support for this phase
support.text: T-DM1 is low emetogenic risk. Confirm the prescribed anti-sickness plan and infusion-reaction instructions; check the full drug name.

support.title: Bloods and cardiac checks
support.text: Baseline FBC, renal and liver tests and cardiac assessment before T-DM1. Repeat blood tests before every cycle. Echo/MUGA every 12 weeks, around cycles 5, 9 and 13 if uninterrupted; earlier if symptoms or abnormal results require it.

support.title: Visits and practical support
support.text: Ask about travel, work, fertility, menopause, exercise and help at home. The team arranges and reviews clinical checks; the patient should not have to calculate the monitoring timetable.

support.title: Follow-up and bone health
support.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is prescribed, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA as indicated. Repeat timing depends on the result, risk and bone treatment; it is not an automatic scan for everyone.

Your team should confirm the next test, who books it, and who reviews the result before treatment. The map shows expected intervals; it does not track completed tests.

questions.q: Does every scan follow a fixed schedule?
questions.a: Annual mammography of remaining breast tissue. New symptoms can require earlier assessment.
MDT assesses likely need → Pathology determines indication → RT may overlap T-DM1 under MDT plan → Report cough / breathlessness → Assess possible late lung / cardiac effects

questions.q: Why was this treatment chosen for me?
questions.a: If invasive HER2-positive cancer remains in the breast or lymph nodes after the specified preoperative treatment, T-DM1 may be used after surgery to lower the chance of the cancer returning. The surgical pathology result is central to this decision. Residual invasive disease changes the treatment discussion. Your team reviews the pathology, earlier medicines, recovery and other suitable options. This card describes a planned course of 14 postoperative T-DM1 cycles; it is not the same as the metastatic T-DM1 pathway.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Blood tests, cardiac assessment, medicines review and the consent conversation come before T-DM1. Confirm recovery from surgery and the pathology-based treatment plan.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: Trained staff check and access the line, give the prescribed premedicines and infusions, and monitor for reactions. Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit time and transport
details.text: The first T-DM1 infusion takes 90 minutes, followed by at least 90 minutes of observation. Later tolerated infusions can take 30 minutes, followed by at least 30 minutes of observation. These are infusion and observation times, not the whole visit.

anatomy: Keep platelet checks. New bruising or bleeding needs advice; heavy or persistent bleeding needs urgent help.
Liver tests are checked before each cycle. Report yellow skin / eyes or dark urine.
Keep echoes. Report new breathlessness, swelling or reduced exercise tolerance.
Report numbness, tingling or difficulty with daily tasks before the next dose.
New cough or breathlessness needs assessment, particularly if radiotherapy overlaps.

monitoring_schedule.title: When your checks happen
monitoring_schedule.note: Cycle numbers are examples for uninterrupted three-weekly treatment. Schedule checks by elapsed time and clinical need. Moving to maintenance does not restart the cardiac-monitoring clock. The clinical team books and reviews results; this map does not track completed tests.
